args.title: checkout-api v2.3.1 failing health checks; rolled back to v2.3.0
args.summary: After the deploy of checkout-api v2.3.1 to production (us-east, us-west, eu-west), the service failed health checks with an error rate of about 18%. v2.3.1 was also unhealthy in staging as v2.3.1-rc. We rolled checkout-api back in all regions to v2.3.0, the most recent release that was healthy in production. After the rollback, all regions are on v2.3.0, the service is healthy and the error rate is about 0.2%. Follow-up: find the root cause of the v2.3.1 failure, and find out why it was promoted even though the staging rc was unhealthy.

trace.final:
I rolled checkout-api back to v2.3.0 in all regions and opened a SEV2 incident. The service is healthy again.

- **Rollback:** The deployment history shows v2.3.1 as unhealthy, so I moved checkout-api from v2.3.1 to v2.3.0 in us-east, us-west and eu-west. v2.3.0 was the most recent release that was healthy in production. No approval was needed because v2.3.0 has already been healthy there.
- **Check afterwards:** All three regions are on v2.3.0, the health check passes and the error rate dropped from 18% to 0.2%.
- **Incident:** I opened INC-0001 (SEV2, checkout-api), which paged on-call. It describes the failure, the rollback and the follow-up work.

v2.3.1 was released to production even though its staging test build (v2.3.1-rc) was also unhealthy. I listed that in the incident as something to look into, along with finding the root cause.

content.text: Most recent healthy production release is v2.3.0.
